P L D 1978 Lahore 85

Before Muhammad Afzal Zullah, J

BABU-Petitioner

versus

DISTRICT JUDGE, SAHIWAL, AND ANOTHER-Respondents

Writ Petition No. 2717 of 1976, decided on 10th
October 1977.

West Pakistan Family Courts Act (XXXV of 1964)-

-- S. 14(i)-Order finally determining question of
setting aside ex parte decree-Held, appealable as a "decision" under
S. I '(I)-Order of District Judge dismissing appeal as incompetent amounting to
refusal to exercise appellate jurisdiction vested in him-Order set aside as
without lawful authority-Constitution of Pakistan (1973), Art. 199.[Ex parts
decree-Appeal (civil)].

Mst. Rushda Zareen v. Muhammad Saleh P L D 1976 Lah.
1327 and Sped Muhammad Raza Shah v. Sayeda Salma Gllant and another P L D 1976
Lah. 1015 ref.

Talat Farooq Sheikh for Petitioner.

Mehr Ghulam All Mubashir for Respondents.

Date of hearing : 10th October 1977.

JUBGMENT

This writ petition arises out of a matrimonial
matter. A learned Family Judge decreed the suit for dissolution of marriage
filed by respondent No. 2 (wife of the petitioner), in absence of the
petitioner through ex parte decree dated 8-7-1976. The petitioner moved an
application before the learned Family Judge under rule 13 of the West Pakistan
Family Courts Rules, 1965. This application was dismissed on 16-10-1976. The
petitioner then filed an appeal under section 14 of the West Pakistan Family
Courts Act, 1964 before the learned District Judge, which was dismissed vide
order dated 27-10-1976 on the ground that such an appeal against the refusal to
set aside an ex pare decree was not competent under section 14 of the Act. This
order has been impugned in this writ petition.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner contends that
the order of the learned Family Judge refusing to set aside the ex parte decree
for dissolution of marriage is different from and independent of the earlier
order resulting in a decree for dissolution of marriage; and thus, the impugned
order of the !learned Family Judge would be treated as a decision covered by
subsection (1) of section 14 of the Act, therefore, the appeal was competent.

3. Learned counsel for the respondent has argued
that decree for dissolution of marriage on any ground other than one specified
in clause (d) of item (viii) of section 2 of the Dissolution of Muslim
Marriages Act, 1939 would not be appealable because of the bar contained in
subsection (2) of section 14 of the Act. And as in this ease the suit was not
decreed on the said ground but on ground of khula', therefore, the appeal was not
competent.

4. Section 14 of the West Pakistan Family Courts
Act, 1964 reads as follows t

"14.-(1) Notwithstanding anything provided In
any other law for the time being in force, a decision given or decree passed by
a Family Court shall be appealable :

(a) to the High Court, where the Family Court is
presided oven by a District Judge, an Additional District Judge or any person
notified by Government to be of the rank and status of a District Judge or an
Additional District Judge ; and

(b) (to the District Court, in any other case).

(2) No appeal shall lie from a decree by a Family
Court

(a) for dissolution of marriage, except in the case
of dissolution for reasons specified in clause (d) of item (viii) of section 2
of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939

(b) for dower not exceeding rupees one thousand ;

(c) for maintenance of rupees twenty-five or less
per month."

5. No doubt decree for dissolution of marriage for
any reason other than that specified in section 2(viii) (d) of the .dissolution
of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939 would not be appealable because of the bar
contained in clause (a) of subsection (2) of section 14 of the Act ; but in the
present case the appeal moved before the learned District Judge was not from
any decree for dissolution of marriage. The appeal was against the order dated
16-10-1976 whereby the learned Family Judge had refused to set aside an ex
parte decree. This order of refusal to set aside an ex parte decree is
undoubtedly independent of and subsequent to the decree for dissolution of
marriage. If the petitioner would have filed two appeals ; (i) against the
decree t'or dissolution of marriage dated 8-7-1976 ; and (ii) against the order
dated 16-10-1976 refusing to set aside the ex parte decree, then the first mentioned
appeal would not be competent because of the bar contained in section 14(2)(x)
of the Act. The second mentioned appeal would be competent because it would not
be against the decree of dissolution of marriage but against a decision by the
learned Family Judge refusing to set aside the earlier decree. It was pointed
out in Mo. Rushda Zareen v. Muhammad Saleh (P L D 1976 Lah. 1327). that the
word "decision" and "decree" are to be given due meaning
when interpreting subsection (1) of section 14. It was accordingly held that n
decree for dissolution of marriage on ground of khula' was not appealable but a
decision with regard to the dower was appealable under section 14(1) of the
West Pakistan Family Courts Act. It was also held in Syed Muhammad Raze Shah v.
Sayeda Salma Gilani and another (P L D 1976 Leh. 1015), that "tire way the
words "decree" and "decision" have been used in section 14,
shows that the word "decision" should be read as ejusdem generis to
the word "decree". If it is so read, it will point out to only such
'decrees' (misprint for 'decision') being appealable which finally determine
the proceedings before the Family Court". In this case the order dated
16--10-1976 undoubtedly finally determined they question of setting aside the
ex parte decree. It was, thus appealable as as 'decision' under section 14(1)
of the West Pakistan Family Courts Act. The order of the learned District Judge
dismissing the appeal as incompetent, A cannot be upheld. It amounts to refusal
to exercise the appellate jurisdiction vested in the District Judge. This
petition accordingly is allowed. The impugned order dated 27-10-1976 is set
aside as without lawful authority and the case is remanded to the learned
District Judge for fresh decision of the appeal in accordance with law. There
shall be no order as to costs.

6. Both the parties are directed to appear before
the learned District Judge on 27-10-1977.

s ,q , _ __ Petition allowed.
